messages:
deploy-bot: Deployment started — release=release-2026-03-21-v3 model=redwood-llm-7b-quant target=change-window-us-east-1 shards=6
alex: rolling traffic: 0% -> 5% now, plan 5% steps every 5m up to 40% (20m ramp)
maya: heads-up: observability panels wired (p50/p95/p99, 5xx rate, infra metrics). link: https://dashboards.redwood/prod/change-window/v3
deploy-bot: healthcheck: shard-1..4 PASS, shard-5 WARN (p95=780ms), shard-6 PASS
sam: noticed a tiny spike in /embed-route 5xx at 5% — not sure if it’s infra or model errors
leo: can we get logs for shard-5?
alex: grabbing logs now — running \`kubectl -n inference logs -l shard=5 --tail=200\`
maya: quick snippet from logs: 
```
E 22:14:03 model-serving: rpc_exception: KVCacheMissError: invalid prefix
W 22:14:04 grpc: retried request, backend=shard-5 status=500
```
sam: KVCacheMissError is new in v3 right? v2 didn't show this
maya: correct — v3 introduced a cache change. p95 trending up from 260 -> 780 in last 6m, p99 also elevated. 5xx % across embed-route is 0.8% -> 1.6% at 5% traffic
alex: recommend pausing ramp. holding at 5% and enabling pin for stable route to v2. any objections?
sam: +1. I vote for immediate pause and pin.
leo: filed infra-ticket INC-4837 for capacity/quota check but this looks like model-side regression
maya: pausing automated ramp. deploy-bot: traffic_hold applied (release=release-2026-03-21-v3, hold_reason=SLO-drift)
alex: can we opt for a quick rollback to v2 while we triage? rollback will reduce customer exposure
sam: propose command to run:
```
/deploy rollback --from release-2026-03-21-v3 --to release-2026-03-07-v2 --scope=change-window-us-east-1
```
maya: initiating rollback now. informing oncall.
deploy-bot: Rollback initiated: from=release-2026-03-21-v3 to=release-2026-03-07-v2 status=in_progress
oncall-bot: Alert: SLO breach detected in change-window-us-east-1 — rolling p95 > 600ms for 2 consecutive windows; severity=warning
leo: infra says no new quota errors, HPA ok. this is a model-level error. grabbing heap/dump from shard-5
alex: thanks. after rollback completes we should watch p95 and 5xx for 10m before closing incident
maya: rollback complete according to deploy-bot, traffic now on v2. deploy-bot: status=done
deploy-bot: Post-deploy health: p50=110ms p95=210ms p99=420ms 5xx_rate=0.12% (back to baseline)
sam: errors dropping to baseline, good. I'll start a quick postmortem doc and add the kernel/kv-cache note
leo: adding follow-up task: investigate cache-change compatibility test gaps (link to taskboard: https://tasks.redwood/BOARD-292)
maya: release notes draft: "v3 rollout paused and rolled back due to kv-cache regression causing elevated p95 and 5xx on embed-route. Rollback to v2 performed. Engineering to root-cause, add integration test for cache behavior, and re-schedule release after fix."
alex: tagging product and customer-success for any user-facing comms. @product @cust-success
maya: also adding a canary test for cache miss spikes in the pipeline before next rollout
sam: +1. will include log signature and remediation steps in the postmortem
leo: closing thread once postmortem link is up. nice quick triage team :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: Incident workflow note: created incident INC-4837, linked runbook runbook://cache-regression, severity=low
